apod.credit: NASA Earth Observatory — Michala Garrison, using Landsat data from the U.S. Geological Survey
apod.explanation: After decades of decline, the world's mangrove forests are making a comeback. A study in Science, based on Landsat imagery from 1984 to 2023, found nearly 2,000 square kilometers of new mangrove growth since 2010, led by expansion in Asia, Australia and South America — reversing losses of nearly 3,000 square kilometers in the decades before. The Landsat images compare Palaw Township in Burma's Myeik District in February 2010 and February 2026, where mangroves have spread into abandoned rice fields and regenerated degraded forest.
apod.title: A Global Rebound for Mangroves

breaking.fact: Bank of America warned the Federal Reserve could raise rates by 50 basis points in December after October CPI came in hotter than expected (core +0.3%, headline +0.4%); its base case stays 25 points, but it raised the risk of a January move too. Fed officials are sounding the same note — Chicago's Goolsbee says the Fed is 'not on track' for 2% inflation, and Governor Bowman says there is 'still work to do'.
breaking.headline: Bank of America warns the Fed could deliver a 50-point hike in December

breaking.headline: IEA says the oil market is back in surplus this quarter, the first since the Iran war began

items.body: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed Friday that a US early-warning radar in Bahrain was destroyed — its first such claim in months — and said the gas carrier reported hit by a mine in the strait this morning was an LPG tanker that had relied on US fighter-jet cover; neither claim has been independently verified, and satellite heat data show no fires at sea after the reported November 11–12 strikes. The tanker hit Wednesday off Ras Al Khaimah is now named as the Sinokor-run Dominica Prosperity, with all 22 crew evacuated, according to UKMTO. Iran is also said to be weighing letting about 25 tankers through in exchange for a blockade lift, though no meeting is scheduled. Flows keep recovering despite the attacks: Asian crude imports through the strait topped 7.4 million barrels a day in October, up from 1.6 million in April, and LNG shipments hit their highest since February. Iranian oil is still getting past the U.S. blockade: 15 Iranian-linked transits crossed in the last seven days against just 4 non-Iranian crossings, though 25 of the 44 tracked crossings could not be attributed.
items.headline: Latest from the Strait

space.headline: Starship Flight 15 goes for the first double catch today
space.body: SpaceX targets a 4:45 p.m. CT liftoff today from Starbase Pad 2 with Booster 22 and Ship 42, both third-generation vehicles. Minutes after launch SpaceX will try to catch the booster at the pad; Ship 42 then deploys 26 Starlink V3 satellites, loops Earth about 14 times over roughly 22 hours, and attempts its own catch back at Starbase around 2:45 p.m. CT Saturday — the first attempt to bring the ship home to land and the first double catch. As of Friday morning the FAA launch license had not yet been issued — the last remaining hurdle — with road closures around Starbase starting at 11 a.m.
Rocket Lab is scheduled to launch its 100th Electron mission at 12:30 a.m. ET Saturday (Nov. 14). The milestone flight comes as Rocket Lab shares slide 5% Friday morning.
space.headline: Rocket Lab's Electron set to fly its 100th mission early Saturday

space.body: Astronomers sifting Vera C. Rubin Observatory data found 2026 ED138, an object 46 times farther from the Sun than Earth that takes 281 years to orbit — and it may be big enough to qualify as a new dwarf planet, only the sixth known. Estimated 370 to 930 miles across, it orbits on a plane tilted nearly 25 degrees, suggesting Neptune's gravity disturbed it; astronomers still need to pin down its size to classify it.
space.headline: Possible new dwarf planet found far beyond Pluto
The blood-brain barrier is a smart filter, not a wall — a clue for Alzheimer's
space.body: Gladstone Institutes researchers tagged 861 mouse blood proteins and found 92 crossed the blood-brain barrier, each ferried to specific brain-cell types — work reported in Cell and covered by Reuters on Friday. One import, the liver protein APOA1, helps maintain connections between neurons; in Alzheimer's-model mice the barrier's APOA1 supply fell and disease signs followed, while boosting it eased them — a possible new treatment angle.

weekInBrief.body: Spot gold fell to about $3,878 an ounce, near a 13-month low, and is down roughly 4% for the week as the 10-year Treasury yield climbed above 5.1% and the dollar strengthened; gold is steadying a little Friday morning near $3,895.

weekInBrief.body: From last Friday's close to Thursday's, the S&P 500 rose 2.9%, the Nasdaq 3.2% and the Dow 2.0%, a strong rebound after the previous week's AI-chip rout — even with Nvidia sliding on its CEO's resignation and the 10-year yield back above 5%. The gains came alongside hotter October inflation data and a sharp fall in gold.
weekInBrief.headline: Stocks rebound for the week despite the Nvidia rout

weekInBrief.body: Google DeepMind launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen on November 12, a fast model built for everyday coding and agentic work, rolling out the same day across the Gemini API, AI Studio, the Gemini app and Google Search, as the AI model race keeps accelerating.
weekInBrief.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its fast AI model for everyday work

weekInBrief.body: October's Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% from September, with core prices up 0.3%, energy up 0.7% and shelter up 0.3% — the latest in a run of hotter-than-expected inflation prints that has markets pricing a December Fed hike, with some chance of a 50-point move. The Bureau of Labor Statistics could not publish 12-month rates for most series because it did not collect October 2025 data during the shutdown.
weekInBrief.headline: October CPI firmer than expected at +0.4%
